candidates.summary: A \left whose delimiter is a command that draws nothing drops the whole \left...\right group instead of reading it as \left., so the content and the \right fence spill into the surrounding row
candidates.failure_scenario: `\left\mathrm{} a \right) b` renders <mrow><mi>a</mi><mo fence stretchy postfix>)</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow>: the ) is a lone fence stretched against the whole row, b included, while `\left. a \right) b` keeps <mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow>. TeX recovers from a bad delimiter with 'Missing delimiter (. inserted)', i.e. as \left., and the new cellEnd table also reads this pair as one group (opensGroup on the tokFence token), so the parser and the cell scan disagree on where the group ends. Base turned the formula into 'invalid math input'; the input is not valid TeX, so this is polish on the crash fix, not a regression
